name: Spinach
family: Amaranthaceae, the amaranth and goosefoot family
grown_as: Annual leaf spinach, picked leaf by leaf or cut young. William's records list 'Santa Cruz F1' (summer, smooth leaves) and 'Giant Winter' (large leaves, overwinters).
habit: A low, spreading rosette 20 to 30 cm across and 15 to 25 cm high. In long summer days it bolts: a single upright stem 30 to 90 cm with smaller leaves and the flowers crowded in its leaf joints.

leaf.arrangement: A rosette from a short stem; alternate on the bolted stem
leaf.outline: Oval to broadly arrow-shaped, the blade 8 to 20 cm long
leaf.base: Blunt to broadly wedge-shaped, in some leaves with two small rounded lobes making a slight arrow shape; stem leaves more clearly arrow-shaped and pointed
leaf.veins: A strong midrib (pale beneath) and a few curving side veins
leaf.surface: Hairless and glossy, smooth to slightly blistered (savoyed) between the veins depending on variety, a little fleshy
leaf.stalk: Fleshy, green, channelled on top, about as long as the blade on outer leaves

flower.form: Tiny green flowers without petals in dense clusters; male and female flowers on separate plants
flower.petals: None: four or five small green sepal-like tepals on male flowers; female flowers just a green tube with fine styles
flower.colour: Green; male clusters yellow-green when the anthers open
flower.centre: Male: four or five yellow stamens; female: four or five white hair-like styles
flower.carried: Male flowers in dense rounded clusters along leafless spikes at the stem top; female flowers in tight clusters in the leaf joints up the stem
flower.season: May to July, when the days are long

fruit: Hard rounded seeds 3 to 4 mm, each inside the dried, closed flower, in clusters up the stem of female plants. Beige to grey-brown and smooth in modern varieties (older prickly-seeded kinds have two to four short horns).
seedling: Two long, narrow, strap-like seed leaves 2 to 3 cm, clearly longer and narrower than the true leaves that follow, which are oval on stalks.
winter: Winter varieties stay as a low rosette through the cold and grow again in spring; summer varieties are gone.

leaf: an oval to slightly arrow-shaped blade with no teeth
a long fleshy stalk about as long as the blade
dark glossy green, a strong midrib and few curving side veins
bloom: tiny green flowers with no petals in a dense cluster
yellow stamens showing on the male cluster
seedling: two long, narrow, strap-like seed leaves
the first true leaves oval on stalks
young: a low rosette of oval leaves on long stalks
crop: a rosette of dark glossy oval leaves on long fleshy stalks
flower: one upright stem with smaller pointed arrow-shaped leaves
small green flower clusters in the leaf joints and at the top
seedhead: clusters of hard round seeds up the yellowing stem

look_alikes: Spinach beet and chard have thicker stalks and broader midribs. Good King Henry and fat hen have mealy, triangular leaves. New Zealand spinach is a sprawling plant with small thick triangular leaves.
